title.narrative: Fostering inclusive economic just recoveries in Nigeria

description.narrative: Our planned work will focus on the explicit and implicit biases of the gender-blind tax system in Nigeria, which are not informed by gender-disaggregated data. Issues such as imposed flat tax rates across all genders within similar informal business categories, regardless of disparities in income, consumption expenditure, and women’s burden of unpaid care, will be critically examined. The failure to acknowledge different tax collection experiences faced by men and women, and the lack of gender-specific grievance redress mechanisms (GRMs), have been identified as root causes of structural macroeconomic barriers to gender equality and women’s rights. The main external impact will be to strengthen the knowledge and capacities of women in the informal sector to collectively and effectively advocate for more gender-sensitive, responsive and transformative tax policies, laws and administrative processes to promote equity and foster inclusive development leveraging on strategic partnerships. The project will be executed on a national scale, with additional focus on three sub-national states: Jigawa, Kaduna and Kano. It will prioritize the advancement of the tax justice campaign with a particular emphasis on bolstering its gender-centric components while complementing existing tax justice initiatives. Our specific objectives include the enhancement of Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs) to effectively address and resolve gendered taxpayer grievances, alongside the development of gender-disaggregated GRM scorecards aimed at monitoring and evaluating complaint resolution, with a specific focus on women taxpayers within the informal sector. At the national level, our efforts will concentrate on advocating for gender equity and responsiveness through active engagement with the Presidential Committee on Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms (PCFPTR), Joint Tax Board and the Nigerian Governors’ Forum.
